events.summary: The Law of the Republic of Tajikistan “On the National Bank of Tajikistan”, No. 722 of 28 June 2011, signed by President Emomali Rahmon, puts every seat on the bank's Board in the President's hands. Article 74(4) says the Chairman of the National Bank and his deputies are appointed to office and released from office by decree of the President, with the decrees submitted to the lower house of parliament for approval, and article 74(3) says the Board's three independent members are approved by the President on the Chairman's proposal. Article 74(6) says the President sets the salary of the Chairman and his deputies.

events.summary: Syria's Basic Monetary Law No. 23 of 2002, issued in Damascus on 17 March 2002 by President Bashar al-Assad, places the bank and its policy-making council under the government. Article 1 says the Monetary and Credit Council works within the general economic directions of the state approved by the Council of Ministers, and sets monetary policy in line with the state's general strategy. Article 8(3) says the Council's decisions are communicated to the Minister of Economy and Foreign Trade, who may suspend for up to seven days any decision he considers contrary to the interest of the state, and if the disagreement continues he must refer the matter to the Council of Ministers to decide. Article 69 says the Governor is appointed, and his service terminated, by decree; article 2 puts the Council's non-bank seats, among them assistant ministers of economy, finance, agriculture and industry and the head of the State Planning Authority, in the gift of a decree on their ministries' proposal; and article 71 says the Minister of Economy and Foreign Trade names the four supervising directors who sit with the Governor on the management committee.
events.source_title: قانون النقد الأساسي — القانون رقم 23 لعام 2002 (Central Bank of Syria)

events.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
events.summary: Bermuda's monetary authority is run by a board the finance minister appoints and can be told what to do by him. The Bermuda Monetary Authority Act 1969 (1969:57), in the consolidated text the Authority publishes, says at section 21(2) that the Minister may give the Authority written general directions that appear to him necessary in the public interest, and that the Authority shall act in accordance with them. Section 4(1)(d) says eleven members of the Board are appointed by the Minister, section 4E(1) says the Minister appoints the Chairman, and section 4E(6) lets the Minister terminate the Chairman's appointment if satisfied he is unable or unfit to discharge his functions. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
events.source_title: Bermuda Monetary Authority Act 1969 (Bermuda Monetary Authority)
events.quote: necessary in the public interest and the Authority shall act in accordance with such directions

events.summary: The Cayman Islands Monetary Authority Law (2020 Revision), revised as at 31 December 2019 and still the principal Act after the Monetary Authority (Amendment and Validation) Act 2024 changed only its fees and regulation-making sections, puts the Authority under the Cabinet. Section 33(1) says the Cabinet may give the Authority written general directions that appear to it necessary in the public interest, and the Authority shall act in accordance with them. Section 12(1) says the Cabinet appoints the directors, section 11(3) says it designates the chairperson and deputy chairperson, section 13(1) says it appoints the managing director, and section 14(3) says the Cabinet, in the public interest, may terminate the appointment of any director. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
events.source_title: Monetary Authority Law (2020 Revision) (Cayman Islands Monetary Authority)
events.quote: give to the Authority, in writing, such general directions as appear to the Cabinet to be necessary in the public interest

events.summary: Under the Central Bank of Solomon Islands Act 2012, which the bank publishes, section 37 says the Minister for Finance may, with the approval of Cabinet, give the Central Bank written directions where the Minister is of the opinion that coordination of monetary and fiscal policies or the public interest requires it, and must publish those directions in the Gazette and lay them before Parliament. Section 41(3) says the other directors of the Board are appointed by the Minister after consultation with the Governor, and section 41(1) says the Governor is appointed by the Governor-General on Cabinet's recommendation. Under section 44 the Governor, Deputy Governor and other Board members may be removed before their term ends only on grounds of permanent incapacity or serious misconduct, and the Governor only on a tribunal's recommendation. The Central Bank of Solomon Islands (Amendment) Act 2023 does not amend sections 37, 41 or 44. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
events.source_title: Central Bank of Solomon Islands Act 2012 (Central Bank of Solomon Islands)
events.quote: may, with the approval of Cabinet, give the Central Bank in writing such directions

events.summary: The National Reserve Bank of Tonga Act, Chapter 16.12, 2020 Revised Edition, puts the bank's board in the government's hands and gives Cabinet the last word on policy disputes. Section 10(1) says the Minister, with the consent of Cabinet, appoints five directors and appoints the Chairman and Deputy Chairman; section 11(1) says the Governor is appointed by Cabinet on the Minister's recommendation; and section 11(3) says the Governor may be removed from office by Cabinet, on the Minister's recommendation made at the Board's request, for permanent incapacity, serious misconduct or failure to perform his duties. Section 50(1) says the Minister may, with the consent of Cabinet, issue the bank written directives, and section 50(4) says that where the Minister and the Board disagree about a policy the Board has determined, the Minister must submit the disagreement to Cabinet to determine the policy to be adopted by the bank. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
events.source_title: National Reserve Bank of Tonga Act, CAP. 16.12, 2020 Revised Edition (Attorney General's Office, Tonga)

events.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
events.summary: Aruba's Central Bank Ordinance (AB 1991 no. GT 32), as amended through AB 2014 no. 5 and published by the Centrale Bank van Aruba in Dutch and in the bank's English translation, keeps the bank under the Governor of Aruba and the Minister of Finance. Section 18 says the president and executive directors are appointed by the Governor from a shortlist of three put up by the Supervisory Board, and that the Governor may suspend or dismiss them by state decree. Section 19(3) says general guidelines for the performance of the duties of the president and executive directors can be set out in a state decree. Section 23 says the chairman of the Supervisory Board is the Government Commissioner, appointed and dismissed by the Governor, that the other supervisory directors are appointed by the Governor, and that they may be suspended or dismissed before the end of their term by the Governor. Section 27(1) says the Government Commissioner supervises the bank's activities on behalf of the Country and acts in accordance with general or specific instructions given by the Minister. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
events.source_title: Central Bank Ordinance (AB 1991 no. GT 32), English translation (Centrale Bank van Aruba)

events.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
events.summary: Cabo Verde's new Organic Law of the Banco de Cabo Verde, Lei n.º 70/X/2026 of 26 January 2026, published in the Boletim Oficial and in force the day after publication, revokes the 2002 Organic Law and says the Government defines monetary and exchange rate policy. Its preamble says the law sets out the bank's functional autonomy with the unequivocal statement that the Government defines monetary and exchange rate policy with the bank's collaboration, and the law lists among the Board of Administration's competences to collaborate with the Government in defining monetary and exchange rate policy, while the bank executes that policy autonomously. The Governor and Vice-Governor are appointed by resolution of the Council of Ministers on the proposal of the member of Government responsible for finance, the non-executive members of the Supervisory Council by the same route, and the executive administrators by resolution of the Council of Ministers on the Governor's proposal. Article 51 says they cannot be moved and may be dismissed only if they cease to meet the requirements of office or commit serious misconduct, by resolution of the Council of Ministers on the finance minister's proposal, with a right of appeal.
events.source_title: Lei n.º 70/X/2026 de 26 de janeiro — Aprova a Lei Orgânica do Banco de Cabo Verde (Boletim Oficial, I Série nº 8)

events.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
events.summary: The Statute of the Banca Centrale della Repubblica di San Marino, Law no. 96 of 29 June 2005, in the consolidated text the bank publishes as in force from 30 November 2025, places every seat on the bank's governing bodies in the hands of the state and gives a committee chaired by the finance minister the job of steering the bank's supervisory work. The President and the five Councillors of the Governing Council are appointed by the Consiglio Grande e Generale, San Marino's parliament, and the Director General is appointed by the Governing Council subject to the parliament's approval. Article 48 says the Committee for Credit and Savings is made up of the Secretary of State for Finance, who chairs it, and two to four people the Congress of State appoints from among its own members, and that the Committee is given the function of directing and orienting banking, financial and insurance supervision. The statute does not say the Committee's directions bind the bank, and this record does not claim that they do. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
events.source_title: Statuto — Legge n. 96 del 29 giugno 2005, testo consolidato in vigore dal 30/11/2025 (Banca Centrale della Repubblica di San Marino)

events.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government direct the bank
events.summary: The Central Bank of The Bahamas Act, 2020 (Act No. 24 of 2020), published in the Extraordinary Official Gazette of 27 July 2020, leaves the whole of the bank's board in the finance minister's gift and makes the bank implement exchange rate policy the minister sets. Paragraph 2(1) of the Schedule says the Governor, the two Deputy Governors and six other directors are all appointed by the Governor-General on the advice of the Minister after consultation with the Board, and paragraph 4(3) says a decision to remove a director or Deputy Governor is made by the Governor-General on the advice of the Minister after consultation with the Board. Section 5(1)(f) says the bank's functions include advising the Minister on the exchange rate policy and implementing the exchange rate policy determined by the Minister. The Central Bank of The Bahamas (Amendment) Act, 2023 does not amend section 5 or paragraphs 2 and 4 of the Schedule. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
events.source_title: Central Bank of The Bahamas Act, 2020 (Act No. 24 of 2020), Extraordinary Official Gazette, 27 July 2020, page 138 (Bahamas Laws On-line)

searched_none.note: Read the Organic Law of the Central Bank of Timor-Leste, Law no. 5/2011, as published by the Banco Central de Timor-Leste (https://www.bancocentral.tl/media/laws/7/7_x67dZ30.pdf). Article 48 puts every seat on the Governing Board in the Prime Minister's hands - he appoints the Governor, the Deputy Governors and the non-executive members on recommendations the law says are non-binding - but article 49 lets him dismiss them only on listed grounds, with an appeal to the courts, and article 3 says the bank's organs cannot seek or receive instructions from any entity including the Government. Held rather than filed: appointment alone, without a power to direct or to remove at will, is nearer the Singapore case that was held than the Kuwait bar.

Read the Centrale Bank-statuut voor Curaçao en Sint Maarten as published in Sint Maarten's Afkondigingsblad 2010 no. 24 (https://repository.officiele-overheidspublicaties.nl/CVDR/CVDR156304/2/xml/i242613.pdf). Article 20 has the president and the two directors appointed by landsbesluit from a joint three-person nomination by the two Ministers of Finance, itself based on a recommendation of at least five members of the Supervisory Board, and suspended or dismissed early only on the Supervisory Board's recommendation by a reasoned landsbesluit; article 18 bars the bank and both its boards from seeking or accepting instructions from the institutions, organs or governments of the two countries. Held rather than filed: no power to direct and no removal at will.

Read the Central Bank of Samoa Act 2015 on PacLII (https://paclii.org/ws/legis/consol_act_2020/cbosa2015174). Section 16(2) has the Head of State, acting on the advice of Cabinet, appoint the Governor and the four non-executive directors, but only on the proposal of an independent panel under section 17 or a selection committee under section 18, and sections 22 and 23 allow removal only on listed grounds. Section 4 says the bank is autonomous, must not take instructions from any other person including a government entity, and that its autonomy must be respected at all times; section 48(1) lets the Minister determine the exchange rate regime in consultation with the bank, and monetary policy is formulated by the bank's Executive Committee. Held rather than filed: with independent selection panels, grounds-based removal and an express no-instructions clause, this is nearer the Singapore case that was held than the Kuwait bar. Samoa's own PDF of the Act (https://www.cbs.gov.ws/media/3339CBS-Act-2015.pdf) is a scan with no text layer.

Looked for Eritrea's central bank statute (the proclamation establishing the Bank of Eritrea, usually cited as Proclamation No. 93/1997) in Russian-free English sources: the Bank of Eritrea has no reachable website (bank.gov.er and bankofertirea.gov.er do not resolve), the Law Library of Congress Eritrea Legal Gazettes collection has neighbouring proclamations (88/1996, 91/1996) but no Bank of Eritrea item, and FAOLEX and ICNL hold only land, environment and public-enterprise laws. No primary text of the statute and no page on which the bank itself names its board could be found, so nothing was filed.
